matchUp.description: Returns back a list of the hero matchups, showing how that hero's win rate is affected with or against other heroes.

heroId.description: The hero id to include in this query, excluding all results that do not include this hero.

heroIds.description: An array of hero ids to include in this query, excluding all results that do not include one of these heroes.

week.description: The week to include in this query, excluding all results that do not include this week. The value is an epoc TimeStamp of the week of data you want. Leaving null gives the current week.

bracketBasicIds.description: An array of rank ids to include in this query, excluding all results that do not include one of these ranks. The value ranges from 0-8 with 0 being unknown MMR and 1-8 is low to high MMR brackets. Example 7 is Divine.

orderBy.description: Id representing how to order dryads and triads. Synergy is STRATZ formula to help determine the best outcome of wins and picks in one. Accepted Inputs : Synergy = 0, Pick = 1, Win = 2, Loss = 3, Disadvantage = 4, Advantage = 5

matchLimit.description: Minimum amount of MatchCount required for a Duo to qualify

skip.description: The amount of data to skip before collecting your query. This is useful for Paging.

take.description: The amount to have returned in your query. The maximum of this is always dynamic. Limit :

claims.contractFinding: The matchUp heroId argument is described as including the hero and excluding results that do not include it; its type is Short.
The schema places heroId1: Short and heroId2: Short on HeroStatsHeroDryadType; descriptions are null.
The schema declares matchCount: Long on HeroStatsHeroDryadType without a field description; matchUp.matchLimit is described as the minimum MatchCount required for a Duo to qualify.
The schema declares winCount: Long on HeroStatsHeroDryadType; description is null.

empiricalReference.reportedObservation: A prior 126-row Puck probe found heroId1=queried hero for all rows; summed winCount/matchCount aligned with winRateHeroId1, and the inverted reading did not.

claims.contractFinding: The matchUp week argument is described as an epoch timestamp of the requested week; the result row week is Int and has no field description.
claims.observedProductionUse: A bucket identifier is multiplied by BUCKET_SEC (604800 seconds) before being sent as week.

claims.contractFinding: The matchUp bracketBasicIds argument is described as filtering to ranks 0-8; the result row field is an enum and has no field description.
claims.observedProductionUse: The query passes the production bracket set: HERALD_GUARDIAN, CRUSADER_ARCHON, LEGEND_ANCIENT, DIVINE_IMMORTAL.

claims.contractFinding: No field description or schema-level invariant states that A→B and B→A matchCount must be equal.
claims.observedFinding: The FIX9 anomaly rows contain unequal reverse-direction matchCount values.

officialQueryExample.querySource: heroStats.matchUp(heroIds, week, bracketBasicIds, take: 200) { heroId vs { heroId1 heroId2 matchCount winCount } }
officialQueryExample.note: This is the project’s production query shape against the official STRATZ endpoint, not a STRATZ-published explanatory example.

documentationAvailability.note: The official docs hostname returned 404 in this run; live schema introspection is the primary official source recorded here.

rootCauseHypotheses.conclusion: The schema does not specify a reverse-direction equality contract; field semantics alone do not explain the asymmetry.

No query-order, pair-only/single-hero, single-hero/matched-batch, or overlapping FIX10 repeatability mismatch was observed in the tested rows. Differences from the older FIX9 batch are reported separately.
Orientation and win-count normalization are reported as observations; they do not by themselves establish why matchCount differs.
The FIX9 aggregate-violating pairs also exceed the unchanged threshold in the current production batch control; persistence is observed but does not explain the asymmetry.

Historical differences are treated as temporal evidence only when current single-hero and matched multi-hero results agree while both differ from FIX9; even then, ingestion provenance and the cause of reverse-direction asymmetry remain unverified.
Per-bucket game totals are summed independently and checked against production aggregation; this does not exclude upstream data defects.
Threshold failures occur in specific pair-weeks and may pass after aggregation; this is a descriptive pattern, not a proven root cause.
No causal category is selected without a documented API contract or a controlled result that excludes alternatives.

evidence.note: Current matched-batch and single-hero outputs agree with each other and have identical differences from FIX9; this does not explain the suspected reverse-direction asymmetry.
The available schema does not specify that reverse-direction matchCount values must be equal.

rootCause.explanation: Pair order, pair-only versus single-hero, and single-hero versus matched production batch controls agree. Historical FIX9 differences are separately attributed only as temporal change evidence when both current query shapes agree; this does not establish why reverse counts differ or a schema equality invariant.
